questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The agency had been robbed by two masked intruders.

options.text: Two masked intruders had rob the agency.
Two masked intruders had been robbed the agency.
Two masked intruders had robbed the agency.
Two masked intruders have been robbing the agency.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Two masked intruders had robbed the agency."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Past Perfect Tense and Active Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a Past Perfect Tense from Active voice to Passive voice:
 
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the verb is changed to its past participle form.
 
 
 
• Structure__: 
 __
 
• Object + had + been + V3 + by + Subject (Passive Voice)__
 
• Subject + had + V3 + Object __(Active Voice)__
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *The things had been arranged by Disha.** *(Passive Voice)
 
• *Disha had arranged the things. *(Active Voice)
 
 
 
• The sentence is in passive voice with the subject 'agency' performing the action 'robbing.'
 
• To convert it into active voice, we need to make the object 'two masked intruders' the subject and use the past participle form of the verb 'rob.'
 
• In this case, we use the past perfect tense 'had been robbed' to show that the action was completed before another past event (day breaking).
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 

Correct sentence: *Two masked intruders had robbed the agency.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.**

The doctors gave him more powerful drugs in the ______ hope that he might recover.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"vain."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Vain"** means having an excessively high opinion of oneself or one's abilities, or **producing no result; useless**. (व्‍यर्थ, बेकार; निष्‍फल, बेनतीजा)

 
 
• **Example**:* She turned away in a **vain**__ attempt to hide her tears.*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, **"vain" **is the correct homophone to use because it means** "without success"** or **"not likely to succeed."**
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

 

**Correct sentence**: *The doctors gave him more powerful drugs in the __**vain**__ hope that he might recover.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: "When"** is a conjunction that is used to introduce a subordinate clause that indicates a point in time or a condition.

 
 
• **Example**: *"**When**__ I wake up, I drink a cup of coffee."*
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "Vein"** refers to a blood vessel that carries blood towards the heart or a streak of a mineral in rock.
 __
 
• **Example**: *"The miner found a **vein**__ of gold in the rock."*
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "Wane" **means to decrease in intensity or power.
 __
 
• **Example**: *"The moon's brightness **wanes**__ as it moves away from the earth."*
 
 

*​* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

 
• In your sentence, the word **"vain" **is used as an adjective to describe the doctors' hope of the patient recovering. "Vain" generally means "having no success or producing no result". Therefore, "in the vain hope" means with a hope that is unlikely to be fulfilled or is not producing the desired result.
 
• In the context of the sentence, it implies that the doctors' actions of giving the patient more powerful drugs – done in the hope that the patient might recover – is likely to be unsuccessful. This phrase sets a rather pessimistic or bleak expectation about the outcome of the situation.
 
• In simpler terms for students, imagine you're attempting to catch raindrops in a sieve. You can keep trying, but we all know that it's not going to hold water. Your efforts would be in "vain" – they won't produce the result you're hoping for. Similarly, in your sentence, the doctors are trying to heal the patient, but the phrase "in the vain hope" suggests they don't really expect to succeed.
 
• Hence, the answer that is marked is absolutely correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in Past Continuous Tense and in Passive Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a Past Continuous Tense from Active voice to Passive voice or Passive to Active Voice:
 
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• Structure: 
 
 
• Object + was/were + being + V3 + by Subject (Passive Voice)__ 
 
• Subject + was/were + v1 + ing + object __(Active Voice)__
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *A song was being sung by Esha.** *(Passive Voice)
 
• *Esha was singing a song. *(Active Voice)​
 
 
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'Tall promises.'​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'each candidate.' 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• 'Were being made' will be changed into 'was making'. 
 
• "Each candidate" is a singular subject so we must "was" with it.
 
• The correct option 4 follows all the above rules and correctly expresses the given sentence in active voice.
